reviews.review: Great game for sandboxing.  Never liked the campaign. I've spent a significant chunk of my life in this game and have no regrets lol
It's a good game, but you don't play it for the campaign.

Just played the official 'Old Man' campaign.  Though 'Played' would be an exaggeration.  I have never encountered such a buggy game ever.

Looking on line at how the missions should have run, over half of them never appeared.  They would frequently get stuck on the same task with no way to complete them.  Looking in forums, lots of other players experienced the same issues.  How the ♥♥♥♥ does a company not test these things?  If most of the user community come across these issues, how did their testers not?  And these are not small bugs.  These are game ending, start again type bugs.

Though there are plenty of small bugs as well.  Dying by touching a rock in the wrong way while swimming.  Spending ages trying to obtain a CSAT uniform only to put it in the inventory of a boat and have it change to the same casual clothes that the character is wearing.

But the main issue is that the tasks do not update correctly, completely destroying the game.

I wouldn't say I have enough playtime to write an accurate review, but based off videos of players who know every keyboard bind and watching some RP scenarios from users like Soviet Womble and jmwFILMS the game is great for those who want a more complex form of Dark RP from Garry's Mod.

Combat is on point with its realism factor. A single bullet can kill you and firing a gun isn't like pointing a laser. If you get hurt after just buying this game then you might end up like me, searching the menus and binds looking for ways to heal yourself or another soldier, getting frustrated with the new language Arma is forcing you down your throat through the keyboard interactions, and looking everything up online.

Overall this game is fun if you invest time into it, I haven't given up and I suggest new players to watch YouTubers who explain rather than try to learn from entertainers.
